bullets.title: S&P -0.7%, Nasdaq -1.0% as rates, oil, and weak jobs data weigh on growth trade
bullets.body: US equities finished notably lower on Sept 1, with S&P 500 down 0.71% and Nasdaq down 1.03% amid a confluence of headwinds: 10-year Treasury yields rose 5bps to 4.79% (19-month high), WTI crude surged 5.2% to $90.78 on US strikes against Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz, and July JOLTS job openings missed at 7.27M (with June revised to the lowest since February). Market breadth was decisively negative at 2.33:1 NYSE and 2.91:1 Nasdaq.

bullets.title: Fed's Barr signals readiness to hike; hawkish regime intact heading into August jobs report
bullets.body: Fed Governor Barr explicitly signaled readiness to hike if inflation doesn't moderate, reinforcing the hawkish tilt from Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks. August payrolls (Friday) are expected soft at +65k headline / +40k private per Morgan Stanley, with unemployment rising to 4.2%; MS cites ~15k drag from Haitian TPS revocations with downside risk. Hedgeye's inflation nowcast tracks August CPI at +3.50% YoY (+14bps sequential acceleration) with Middle East energy disruption as the primary driver.

bullets.title: Oil +5% on Iran strike; diesel at 4-month high with refining margins at record $106/bbl
bullets.body: US airstrikes against Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz drove WTI up 5.2% to $90.78, with diesel hitting a four-month high and refining margins reaching a record $106/barrel. Piper's technical setup sees WTI breaking above $88 with targets of $93.5–$97. Rising input costs from Iran supply chain disruption compound AI buildout and tariff-driven cost pressures already showing up in ISM/PMI data.

bullets.title: Quant regime: risk-off internals persist despite 'Normal Expansion' macro backdrop
bullets.body: GS quant notes that 78% of weeks since late June have shown risk-off market internals — historically anomalous for a Normal Expansion regime. Value and Low Volatility factors are now leading, reversing the Growth/Momentum dominance of 1H26. The catalyst for a rotation back to risk-on would be easing uncertainty about AI investment profitability or a softer financial conditions path; Warsh's commentary is seen extending the near-term risk-off trend.

bullets.title: Software outperformed NDX by >11% in August; sustainability debated into September
bullets.body: GS trading desk reports software beat NDX by more than 11% for back-to-back months, driven by positioning, technicals, and an easing AI bear case. The key September debate is whether application software can sustain gains given two-way earnings (INTU/HUBS bear vs. MSFT/CRM bull camps). CRM, TEAM, NOW, PSKY, and DASH are flagged as overbought on 14-day RSI, while APP and GEV are oversold. Key September catalysts include CRWD, CRM, HUBS, and INTU analyst days plus GS Communacopia + Tech Conf (9/8–11) with NVDA CEO, AVGO CEO, OpenAI CFO, and MSFT CFO keynotes.

bullets.title: AI/Power trade under pressure: TX/PA/OH data center policy + Musk solar supply shock
bullets.body: GS flags the AI/Power trade under pressure following data center policy developments in Texas, Pennsylvania, and Ohio, with midterm election rhetoric adding to setup uncertainty. Separately, Elon Musk announced Tesla and SpaceX are each building 100 GW/yr solar capacity (incremental to prior 100 GW plans), which Wells Fargo says creates significant supply pressure and negative long-term pricing impact for FSLR. The AI capex boom itself is cited by multiple sources as a driver of inflation risk and tighter financial conditions.

bullets.title: 22V: AI capex scale raises inflation/rate risk; favors cash-return and high-AI-usage software over broadening trade
bullets.body: 22V argues that strong underlying demand, tight labor, and persistent supply shocks are elevating the risk that the base case of 'slower growth, less-bad inflation' breaks toward higher inflation and tighter financial conditions. AI-related capex at scale is itself seen as an inflationary force. The desk is moving away from the broadening/small-cap trade and toward cash return and high-AI-usage services/software.

bullets.title: GS hedge fund August: Fundamental L/S flat, Systematic L/S +3%; gross leverage rises for first time in 3 months
bullets.body: Global Fundamental L/S managers finished flat in August, underperforming the market, while Systematic L/S posted +3.0%, its best month YTD. Overall book gross leverage rose for the first time in three months. Net buying was concentrated in North America and EM Asia; Communication Services, Financials, and Materials were the most net-bought US sectors.

bullets.title: Manufacturing PMI seeing local peak; input cost pressures elevated, firms passing through
bullets.body: Manufacturing PMIs show a local peak following robust reacceleration since last fall, but forward indicators suggest demand remains positive. Backlogs of work rose for a sixth consecutive month and firms are increasingly able to pass cost-push shocks to customers. ISM new orders slowed to 53.7 from 56.8 and the employment sub-index came in at 51.2; 22% of manufacturing GDP contracted in August vs. 20% in July, with rising input costs from AI buildout, Iran disruption, and tariff policy all cited.

bullets.title: Anthropic inks $35B compute deal with Lambda/NVDA; SBE Energy IPO filed at $50B+ valuation
bullets.body: Anthropic agreed to a $35B computing deal with Lambda cloud provider backed by NVDA, with HUT developing a related Texas data center. NVDA- and SoftBank-backed SBE Energy separately filed for an IPO targeting a $5–7B raise at a $50B+ valuation for data center buildout. OpenAI CFO noted +35% revenue run rate QTD and is targeting a public offering in 2027 or sooner; Anthropic's pre-IPO tokenized equity implies a $1.925T market cap.

bullets.title: August monthly recap: S&P +2.62%, Nasdaq +3.93%; software (IGV) +16.3%, PLTR +51.5%, NVDA +9.8%
bullets.body: August delivered broad gains led by tech: IGV software ETF +16.3%, S&P Tech sector +6.19%, SOX +2.0%. PLTR surged 51.5% on AI commercial demand reacceleration; TSLA +18.2%, MSFT +9.2%, NVDA +9.8% among Mag 7 leaders. Fed expectations tilted hawkish into September; Chair Warsh's remarks leaned hawkish on inflation. Taiwan (+7.0%) and Korea (+6.9%) led Asia on AI supply chain strength.

bullets.title: 10-year JGB hits 3% (30-year high); global yields surging on Iran, oil, and AI capex concerns
bullets.body: The 10-year JGB yield reached 3%, a 30-year high, as part of a broad global yield surge. US 10-year rose to 4.79% (+5bps on the day), and the 30-year to 5.27% (+3bps). The REIT sector cited global bond yields surging on Iran tensions, oil price pressures, and the AI capex boom as the key driver of the rate backup. Data Center REITs were the worst YTD REIT performer, down 1.60%.

bullets.title: Consumer Discretionary (XLY) technically deteriorating; only 36% of constituents above 50-day MA
bullets.body: Technical analysis shows XLY momentum rolling lower from an early-2025 peak, with only 36% of constituents above the 50-day MA and 40% above the 200-day MA. 59% of sector stocks have weak/poor technical scores. Separately, GS notes retail showing consumer spending slowdown signs, with TJX/BURL off-price weakness leading a sell-off; the GS Retail Conference (9/14–15) will feature WMT and TJX with hints that 3Q improved vs. 2Q.

bullets.title: Hedgeye CPI nowcast: August tracking +3.50% YoY (+14bps acceleration); September flat at +3.49%
bullets.body: Hedgeye's monthly inflation nowcast — which claims 90% directional accuracy — calls for August headline CPI at +3.50% YoY, a +14bps sequential acceleration driven by Middle East energy market disruption. September is projected to be nearly flat at +3.49% YoY. August CPI releases September 11th; September CPI on October 14th.

bullets.title: Taiwan August: TWSE +7%, FII net bought $7.6B; DC infrastructure delivery seen as bottleneck
bullets.body: Taiwan equities rebounded 7.0% in August with MSCI Taiwan gaining 6.3% in USD on $7.6B of FII net buying. GPU and ASIC demand described as very strong; smartphones the only weak spot. DC infrastructure delivery is flagged as a potential bottleneck, with HVDC power rack ramping in 4Q26/1Q27. MediaTek's TPU opportunity is projected at an $80–100B annual run-rate by 2030, likely taking majority unit share in TPUv8 and becoming primary vendor for TPUv9.
